title: HITCON CTF 2026 — Investigation Update
description:
Thank you all for your patience!

During HITCON CTF 2026, we received reports that some teams may have created additional accounts (sub-accounts) to gain an unfair competitive advantage. As a result, we needed additional time to investigate these reports before finalizing the competition results.

We would like to share our findings and the actions we have taken.

## 1. Drone Battle — Sub-Account Violations

The rules of **Drone Battle** explicitly stated that each team was allowed to use only one account.

However, our investigation found clear evidence that:

- **ForgottenDestiny** was a sub-account of **SuperDiceCodeLovers**.
- **lululala** was a sub-account of **TeamH4C**.

We contacted both teams to verify our findings, and **both teams accepted the outcome of our investigation**.

We understand that both are large teams with members from diverse backgrounds, and that managing such teams can be challenging. We also appreciate that both teams actively cooperated with our investigation after the competition.

Nevertheless, to uphold the competition rules and ensure fairness for all participants, we regret that we must **disqualify SuperDiceCodeLovers and TeamH4C**.

Additionally, during the competition, we received reports that two other accounts, **gyu** and **不知归**, might have been created as sub-accounts to manipulate the results of Drone Battle.

Although we do not have conclusive evidence linking these accounts to any specific teams, our review of the relevant logs and Drone Battle replays revealed behavior that we determined to be detrimental to the fairness of the competition.

Therefore, we have decided to **disqualify both gyu and 不知归**.

### KoH Score Adjustments

Following these disqualifications, we have recalculated the Drone Battle King of the Hill (KoH) scores and updated the scoreboard accordingly.

We recognize that many teams made strategic decisions during the competition based on the actions of other teams. Replaying all rounds would not necessarily reproduce the same competitive environment or guarantee a fairer outcome.

After careful consideration, we decided to **adjust only the KoH scores rather than rerun the rounds**.

## 2. VulCreator & VulCreator-Revenge — Instance Limit Violations

The challenges **VulCreator** and **VulCreator-Revenge** had instance limits of **10 and 3**, respectively.

Although the challenge rules did not explicitly state that each team could only use one account, we believe that using sub-accounts to bypass these limits violates the principle of fair competition.

These limits were intentionally established as part of the challenge design, and circumventing them through additional accounts provides an unfair advantage over teams that followed the intended restrictions.

After reviewing the relevant logs, we found clear evidence that **SaturnX** and **熊貓特戰隊** used additional accounts to obtain instances beyond the specified limits.

As a result, we have decided to revoke the following points:

- **SaturnX:** Points earned on both **VulCreator** and **VulCreator-Revenge**.
- **熊貓特戰隊:** Points earned on **VulCreator**.

These adjustments have also been reflected on the scoreboard.

## 3. Investigation of Overlapping IP Addresses

During our investigation, we also identified several teams whose activities originated from overlapping IP addresses.

We contacted the teams involved to request clarification and have since received reasonable explanations for these overlaps.

We would like to thank all the teams who promptly responded to our inquiries and actively cooperated with our investigation. Your cooperation helped us better understand the circumstances and complete our review.

## 4. Scoreboard Adjustments

In addition to the adjustments mentioned above, **the scores for all Jeopardy challenges have been recalculated after excluding disqualified teams from the scoring calculations**.

The scoreboard has been updated to reflect these changes.

title: HITCON CTF 2026 Has Ended!
description:
# 🏁 HITCON CTF 2026 Has Ended!

**HITCON CTF 2026 has officially come to an end!** 🎉

Thank you all for participating! We hope you enjoyed the challenges and had a great time hacking with us.

**📢 Final Rankings and Results**

Please note that some challenge scores are still under review, so **the current scoreboard rankings are not yet final and may be subject to change**.

Once the scores have been verified, we will announce the official final results and contact the winning teams to request their write-ups.

Thank you for your patience and understanding!

Once again, thank you for being part of HITCON CTF 2026. We hope to see you again next year!

— HITCON CTF Team

description:
# 🚩 HITCON CTF 2026 Has Begun!

Welcome to **HITCON CTF 2026**! 🎉

The competition has officially started! We hope you enjoy the challenges we've prepared and have a great time hacking. Good luck, have fun, and happy hacking!

**📢 Upcoming Challenge Releases**

More challenges will be released in two additional batches:

- **12 hours after the start:** October 24, 2026, at 02:00 UTC
- **24 hours after the start:** October 24, 2026, at 14:00 UTC

**👑 King of the Hill (KotH)**

We also have a **King of the Hill** challenge coming up!

- **Expected start:** October 24, 2026, at 02:00 UTC (12 hours after the competition begins)
- **Expected end:** October 25, 2026, at 14:00 UTC (competition ends)

The KotH challenge is expected to remain active until the end of the competition. Stay tuned for more details!

Thank you all for participating in HITCON CTF 2026. We hope you have an amazing 48 hours!

**Happy hacking! 🔥**

— HITCON CTF Team
